requirement:
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.**

**Implementation**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs:43-182) builds the mandatory set only from these sources:
  - the subject itself,
  - the subject's `{cite}` targets,
  - `{impl}`/`{test}` sites and anchors that point at the subject,
  - the terminology those inputs bring in.
- It never reads `evidence/<subject>.json`, so an earlier record's inputs, determination and rationale cannot enter the mandatory set. The comment "Existing evidence only decides whether to reassess; its inputs are not carried forward" matches the code.
- `recorded: Vec::new()` starts empty. `assess` (src/authoring/mod.rs:449-579) calls `record_inputs` only for inputs actually delivered: the mandatory set plus tool deliveries, and only after a provider response. The evidence is built from `sources.recorded_inputs()`. A new record therefore holds only what was supplied in the new run, and stale or removed sources cannot block or shape reassessment.
- `author_all_with_options` (src/authoring/batch.rs:33-185) uses `LoadedDetailEvidence::load` and its `EvidenceState` solely to decide whether a subject needs assessment. Valid, Fixme and DeterminationFalse records are left unchanged. It passes only the subject name to `prepare_assessment`, so the old record's content is not forwarded to the model.
- `omit_generated_evidence`, `generated_evidence_path` and `generated_evidence_selector` keep generated `evidence/` content, including symlink aliases, out of the mandatory set by default. Explicit workspace allow and disallow rules are respected. `source_input` and `prepare` enforce read denial. The `{impl}` markers are present on all of these.
- `configured_assessment` (the single-subject path) does not read old evidence either.

**Tests** (src/authoring/inputs.rs)
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (481-566) writes an old record that contains a false determination, a rationale and a `notes.txt` input. It asserts that:
  - the mandatory inputs omit `notes.txt` and the old rationale,
  - the recorded inputs are empty.
- `unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment` (568-596) puts missing files, a removed Rust item and a removed requirement in the old record. `prepare` still succeeds, and the result is exactly the subject input.
- `earlier_evidence_inputs_and_judgments_are_not_carried_forward` (598-625) asserts that the supplied inputs contain no `evidence/` path, no old source and no old judgment. It also asserts that the old file is left unchanged.
- Related tests cover generated-evidence omission, default exclusion, symlink aliases, explicit allow and disallow aborts (inputs.rs:899-991, tools.rs:823-948).

**Gaps and risks**
- There is no end-to-end test through `assess` or the batch path that checks the final persisted record. `prepare` and `recorded_inputs` are tested, and the code path from them to the record is short.
- With an explicit workspace allow of `evidence/`, the model's tools could read an old record. That follows `requirements.configuration.evidence_paths` and `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, not this requirement.
- Neither affects the judgment.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
